rtti.evidence: config/arm9/overlays/ov006/relocs.txt carries exactly three relocations whose source is the record itself: 0x0213d350 -> 0x0209a764 (main), 0x0213d354 -> 0x0213d35c, 0x0213d358 -> 0x0213bc64. The bytes at 0x0213d35c are the NUL-terminated string 14dScMgMemory2_c, named _ZTS14dScMgMemory2_c in ov006's own symbols.txt.

base_evidence: The __si_class_type_info record at 0x0213d350 has +0x08 = 0x0213bc64. ov006's symbols.txt names 0x0213bc64 _ZTI19dScMgSingle3DBase_c, whose name pointer 0x0213bd00 holds the NUL-terminated string 19dScMgSingle3DBase_c. build/rtti.json continues the chain: dScMgSingle3DBase_c -> dScMgBase_c (ov004 0x020bbf6c) -> dScene_c (arm9 0x020914d4) -> dBase_c (arm9 0x02086e78) -> fBase_c (arm9 0x02086d70). SIX classes counting self, which is what fixes the compiler-only row count at 2 x 6 + 1 = 13.

vtable.extent_evidence: Two independent sources agree on 36. (1) relocs.txt has a relocation whose source is the word itself for every address from 0x0213d4d4 through 0x0213d560 inclusive, and none at 0x0213d564: (0x0213d560 - 0x0213d4d4) / 4 + 1 = 36. (2) tools/rtti_vtables.py --own dScMgMemory2_c reports 36 slots, base 36. The word at 0x0213d564 is named data_ov006_0213d564 in symbols.txt and is only ever LOADED FROM, by code at 0x020f820c, 0x020f8a14 and 0x020f8cf8 -- a following table, not a trailing slot, and there are no trailing nulls to qualify. Reading the extent from the next symbols.txt row happens to agree here (0x0213d564 - 0x0213d4d4 = 0x90 = 36 slots), but the relocation walk is what proves it.

overrides.name: InitResources
overrides.body: Loads the minigame's resources and builds the scene; 0x120 bytes, ending where the factory begins.

overrides.name: Behavior
overrides.body: Per-frame tick. Dispatches through the class's own main-state PMF table, the one __sinit_ov006_021314e4 fills with StateSetup / StatePlay / StateJudge / StateResult / StateExit.

overrides.name: Render
overrides.body: Draws the card, cursor and message layers, then chains to the inherited render path.

overrides.name: D1 destructor
overrides.body: Destroys the 0x270-byte shared table at this+0x4f38 through func_ov006_020c1c64, stores vptr (int)&_ZTV14dScMgMemory2_c[2], destroys the inherited Particle::SysTracker, then calls _ZN11dScMgBase_cD2Ev at 0x020b29c0.

overrides.name: D0 deleting destructor
overrides.body: Runs the same chain as D1 and then deallocates through Memory::Deallocate at 0x0203c1e8. The cartridge places D0 ABOVE D1, i.e. D1 is the lower address -- the reproducible direction, so the pair stays inside the licensed run.

overrides.name: OnYoshiTryEat
overrides.body: Minigame-specific reaction to Yoshi's tongue; 0x60 bytes.

overrides.name: OnGroundPounded
overrides.body: 0x14 bytes, the shortest of the eight overrides.

non_virtual.evidence: Forty-three of the 51 member bodies are not vtable targets: no word in 0x0213d4cc..0x0213d564 relocates to any of their addresses. What makes them dScMgMemory2_c members rather than free helpers is their receiver use plus their membership in the four member-function-pointer tables __sinit_ov006_021314e4 builds -- main, result, card and player -- and in the separate ten-entry round table, which independently fixes RoundStart through RoundReveal order.

factory.evidence: tools/opnew_sizes.py resolves ov006:0x020f75dc to an inline_store of 21520 = 0x5410 into _ZN7fBase_cnwEj, with vtable 0x0213d4d4 and size_confidence exact. include/dScMgMemory2_c.h carries the matching compile-time assert sizeof(dScMgMemory2_c) == 0x5410, so the header and the cartridge agree.

size_evidence.member_extent: The header's field list runs from mShared at 0x4f38 (0x270 bytes, size-asserted) through mCards[20] at 0x51a8 (0x18 stride), mPlayers[3] at 0x5388 (0x14 stride), mCursor at 0x53c4 (0x10) and the state scalars, ending with pad_540d[3] at 0x540d -- exactly 0x5410.

fields.name: mShared
fields.evidence: Both destructors call func_ov006_020c1c64 with this+0x4f38, and four sibling dScMgSingle3DBase_c scenes carry the same 0x270 table. NEITHER dScMgMemory_c NOR dScMgMemory2_c reads inside it, so no field of it is named.

fields.name: mCards[20]
fields.evidence: CardMove, CardSelect, CardFlipUp, CardFlipDown, CardWait, CardIdle and CardFlyAway index this+0x51a8 with a 0x18 stride; ShuffleCards walks all twenty.

fields.name: mPlayers[3]
fields.evidence: PlayerMove, PlayerDrop, PlayerWait and InitPlayers index this+0x5388 with a 0x14 stride over three elements.

fields.name: mCursor
fields.evidence: DrawCursor, UpdateCursor, ShowCursor and HideCursor address this+0x53c4; DrawCursor gates on the byte at this+0x53d2.

fields.name: mState
fields.evidence: StateSetup, StatePlay, StateJudge, StateResult and StateExit write it; Behavior dispatches on it.

fields.name: mSubstate
fields.evidence: The round, result and card sub-state machines write it.

fields.name: mMessageVisible
fields.evidence: DrawMessage returns early unless the byte at this+0x540b is non-zero.

unproven: Original source spellings for the 43 address-only member bodies and for every field name above. The ROM proves ownership, stride and width; the names are descriptive coinage, disclosed here, in config/tu_manifest.d/ov006/dScMgMemory2_c.json and in symbols/actor_renames.tsv.
Any field inside the 0x270-byte mShared table. Neither dScMgMemory_c nor dScMgMemory2_c reads inside it, so borrowing a sibling's field names would assert bytes this class never touches.

The original translation-unit cut at the LEFT edge. build/tu_map.json rates both boundaries medium and reports ov006 under-segmented; the run is contiguous and the factory is unique to the class, but adjacency alone does not prove the original one-to-one file cut.

Ownership of the non-.text sections. The four PMF tables, the resource and static data, _ZTV / _ZTI / _ZTS, __sinit_ov006_021314e4 and the 0x021423a8..0x02142490 BSS stay ROM-gap owned; the promotion claims .text only.
